title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: KENDRA'S TOAST
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Kendra Mayfield, a meat plant electrician in Sioux Falls, South Dakota.
She can rewire a giant freezer in the dark, but a crowd makes her knees shake.
Then her Grandma Ruth asked her to give the toast at her ninetieth birthday party.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: SAYING YES
segments.quote: The only courage that matters is the kind that gets you from one moment to the next.
segments.author: Mignon McLaughlin
lines: Kendra hid in the break room with nine excuses.
Her cousin texted her a line from the writer Mignon McLaughlin:
The only courage that matters is the kind that gets you from one moment to the next.
So she stopped picturing the whole party, called Grandma back, and said one word. Yes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE WRONG NUMBER
segments.quote: The art of conversation is the art of hearing as well as of being heard.
segments.author: William Hazlitt
lines: Kendra only knew Grandma as the lady with the good pie.
On the drive over, a radio host read the English writer William Hazlitt:
The art of conversation is the art of hearing as well as of being heard.
So she brought a notebook, asked one question, and listened for four hours.
In nineteen fifty-five, Grandma was a phone operator. Grandpa Walt called the wrong number three times. On purpose.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: BIG WORDS
segments.quote: Don't use words too big for the subject.
segments.author: C. S. Lewis
lines: Kendra wrote six pages of fancy words like indefatigable.
Her husband Luis showed her advice from the writer C. S. Lewis:
Don't use words too big for the subject.
So she cut it down to one card. Grandma wasn't indefatigable. She was tough as an old boot.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE LOCKER ROOM
segments.quote: You might as well fall flat on your face as lean over too far backward.
segments.author: James Thurber
lines: She practiced in the plant locker room, stiff as a fuse box.
Her coworker Hector said she sounded like a safety video, and read her the funny writer James Thurber:
You might as well fall flat on your face as lean over too far backward.
So she quit trying to be perfect. She tripped on a word, laughed, and finally sounded like herself.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE DEAD MIC
segments.quote: Words are, of course, the most powerful drug used by mankind.
segments.author: Rudyard Kipling
lines: Saturday at the VFW hall, sixty people came. Halfway through her first line, the microphone died.
She could fix it. Then she remembered the British writer Rudyard Kipling:
Words are, of course, the most powerful drug used by mankind.
So she set the mic down, walked to Grandma's table, and told the wrong number story. The hall laughed. Grandma turned pink.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE TOAST
segments.quote: If you would be loved, love, and be loveable.
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: For the ending, she raised her glass with the Benjamin Franklin line stitched on Grandma's kitchen pillow:
If you would be loved, love, and be loveable.
Then she asked everyone Grandma ever helped to stand. All sixty stood.
Grandma Ruth wiped her eyes and said, Fine. You're doing my hundredth.

segments.head: GOOD NIGHT
segments.quote: Say yes. Listen. Keep it plain. Laugh. Speak. Love.
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: So, say yes one moment at a time, listen, keep it plain, laugh when you trip, speak from the heart, and love out loud.
Me? I gave a toast at my brother's wedding once. I thanked the wrong bride.
Happy Thanksgiving. I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
